In choosing alternative potential development scenarios for discussion and analysis in this statement, it was felt that the tonnage rates stipulated in the amended leases should be treated as a minimum production or low level scenario. Higher levels of production would depend primarily upon availabity of additional equipment to that now planned, thereby placing practical limits on the range of production which might realistically be expected. For purposes of discussion a second or high level development scenario has been chosen using a rate of 26 million tons of coal annually from Tracts II and III by 1992. Reserves would be exhausted by the year 2030 at the high level, and by 2070 at the low level. These two scenarios assume that the coal is to be transported from the region by rail.
The most likely scenario under present conditions is the low level development specified in the leases. Consequently this statement will analyze the impacts of this scenario in greatest detail. The high level is less likely and consequently will be treated in lesser detail.
The third level of development which is analyzed in this statement concerns a combination of low level development plus energy conversion. No plans exist for realization of a energy conversion facility; consequently the impact analysis for this third scenario will not be extensive. Should plans for an energy conversion facility be submitted a detailed EIS would be required on the proposal. At this level a total of 14 million tons could be mined from the two tracts for rail shipment only, while an additional 6.5 million tons per year could be mined for energy conversion. This level of mining would slightly exceed the minimum production requirements of the leases.
